_doc: OPTIONAL GATES, on top of profiles.registration.json (identical apart
from this block and this note). Supplying a check does not make it
mandatory; this file is the separate decision that does. Inactive.
member and acceptance require the full backend suite; integration and
acceptance also require the docs build and a Bench review verdict of
APPROVE bound to the exact head (review: bench). Because every intent
asks for the same names at root `source`, a review's own bench-backend
run is evidence the acceptance gate can read, provided it ran against
the commit about to merge. bench records which run reviewed; it does
NOT establish that the reviewer is independent of the author, and
separate-reviewer is not used because one GitHub account cannot
formally review its own pull request.
bench-backend refuses any skipped test and is prepared by
`verify/preflight backend` (node + markdown-it-py), so a service PATH
without node holds the gate as prepare-failed rather than passing
`OK (skipped=121)`. This example has no PR-head (`review` root)
variant: a review's bench-backend is the card's branch tip, not the
pinned pull request head. Do not activate a gate until these checks
have run in the operator's own environment.
bench-docs is gated: on a machine whose docs interpreter lacks
markdown-it-py it is prepare-failed every time and the gate holds.
That is the intended reading — prepare the interpreter, do not drop
the requirement to get a merge through.
bench-browser is deliberately not required: on a host whose Chromium
cannot start its sandbox it is prepare-failed every time, and a gate on
it would refuse every merge. Add it once a host has shown it passing.
Evidence must be bound to a clean committed head: commit, then ask.
overrides stay off.
